description: Derives the convention-D q-AND amplitude rather than z-swapping it. Splitting the published Phi by parity in sqrt(q) gives Phi = A z^2 + B z with A = (q-1)^2(q+1)^2/(2q) and B = (q-1)(q^2+q+1)/(2(q+1)), both RATIONAL in q, and the decomposition is unique because z_C is not in Q(q). The convention enters through z alone, so Phi_D = A z_D^2 + B z_D = q^3(q-1)(q^6+2q^5+q^4-q^3+q^2+q+1) / (2(q+1)(q^2+1)^2). Its sextic has no real roots, so Phi_D vanishes on (0,inf) only at q = 1. The convention-C threshold at q ~ 0.4656, published as a phase reversal of the q-AND, does not exist under the canonical convention. At q0 both amplitudes are positive (0.0495 C, 0.0625 D), so the stability verdict survives.
caveats: Both entries are DERIVED, not z-swapped: each is a z-polynomial with Q(q) coefficients and no constant term (Phi = B z + A z^2, P_77 = z + h z^2), reconstructed symbolically against the published closed forms, so the convention enters through z alone. An earlier revision reported P_77 as conditional because the constant (q-1)/(q+1) looked unstructured; it is h*z_C^2 exactly. NOT covered here: the off-diagonal P_66, whose published form carries q^{7/2} and which this probe does not decompose.
